sources.title: The Orbital Mechanics of Space Elevator Launch Systems

locations.finding: Departing spacecraft energy comes from Earth rotation through the anchored tether; it is not created by a negative work segment.
a(r)=-mu/r^2+omega^2*r; integrating yields rotating effective-potential work and free sliding radial velocity. The paper uses geocentric radius rp, not height.
epsilon=|v|^2/2-mu/rp; zero-radial-speed Tier 0 escape threshold rp=(2mu/omega^2)^(1/3), about53123km.
Planetary orbit-insertion delta-v is explicitly excluded from the paper analysis.

extractable_parameters: Finite radial-release speed envelope and release geometry
cannot_extrapolate: No validated material or climber throughput
Propellant-free departure is not propellant-free lunar capture or landing
Daily planetary launch capability requires the specific Tier3 steerable ramp; it is not a feature of every tether
Apex radius100000km in this paper is not the MCM100000km tether height

locations.finding: Large-vehicle plumes increase excavation, thermal and ejecta risks. The campaign used1m^2 candidate coupons and15hot-fire tests; this is material testing, not terminal cadence validation.

Atmospheric1g rocket testing cannot reproduce the lunar vacuum/one-sixth-g plume interaction; the experiment approximates selected material challenges.

Need to distinguish terrestrial tests from lunar conditions

constant_sources.boundary: Rounded fact-sheet constants; not a precision ephemeris
Mean orbital values; no departure-date ephemeris or landing-site trajectory

key_model_corrections.correction: Interpret task100000km tether as height. Use r_apex=R_E+100000km; distinguish source papers using apex geocentric radius.

Use Phi_eff=-mu/r-omega^2*r^2/2. Calculate positive drive work to GEO and braking beyond GEO separately. Without explicit regeneration, grid draw does not receive a negative-work credit. Energy and angular momentum are exchanged with Earth rotation via tether torque.

Release-state inertial energy and vector determine feasible lunar transfers. A high apex with positive Earth-centered energy is not automatically a low-delta-v lunar arrival. Solve release longitude/time, lunar phase/inclination and capture/descent together before calibrating delta-v, flight time or propellant.

Earth launch rated payload, elevator lifted mass, transfer initial mass, lunar-orbit arrival mass and landed usable cargo are different quantities. beta=1.5 is a scenario, not a derived physical constant. Rocket-equation zero-dry-mass curves are only optimistic lower bounds for a declared total propulsive delta-v.

Keep unverified terminal capacity as a named scenario. Distinguish lunar vicinity arrival, soft landing, unloading, storage and point-of-use delivery. Construction cargo and pad/handler/road capacity consume mass and time.
